fixes.explanation: Yes, God says, “For I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.” A sign points at something beyond itself. Ezekiel's packing, wall digging and face covering are all pointing at what's coming for Jerusalem. He's the signpost, and the explanation comes the next morning.

Yes, and the text says it right away: “So I did as I was commanded.” Ezekiel brings the bags out by day, digs through the wall in the evening and carries his things out at dusk. Digging through a wall by hand is not a normal evening, and he did it anyway. That's obedience with dirt under the fingernails.

That's it. God says, “This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are there.” A burden here is a heavy message from the LORD. Ezekiel acts it out as they watch, but the message is about the prince and the people in Jerusalem.

That makes sense, since they're the ones watching. But God points somewhere else: “This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are there.” The word “there” means Jerusalem, not the crowd standing around Ezekiel. The ones watching are not the ones the message is about.

God says something very different. He'll bring the prince to Babylon, “yet he will not see it, and there he will die.” So the prince does not see Babylon with his own eyes. It's a heavy verse, and I think it's a hard one to sit with.

That's it. God tells Ezekiel, “…eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with quivering and anxiety.” This time there's no wall and no bags. It's just a man at a meal, shaking. Even eating bread becomes part of the message.

Yes. God says, “I will put an end to this proverb, and in Israel they will no longer recite it.” He doesn't just argue with it. He ends it. Then He tells Ezekiel to say, “The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled.”

Yes, God says, “…because I, the LORD, will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be fulfilled without delay.” Think of the proverb about the days going by and every vision failing. Here God says His word won't be held up. The people were saying it was taking forever, and this is the answer.
